messages:
maya: PSA — Acme just asked for 'consumption smoothing' to avoid hard throttles on short spikes. They described a 5m smoothing window + temporary burst credit. Asking for a PRD and scope call. pinging product + eng.
jules: Understood. Can we clarify must-haves vs nice-to-haves? Tentative ACs: opt-in per tenant, visible in Console, billing tie to credits. What can we ship in 2 sprints? :thinking_face:
dmitri: Need traffic samples to validate. Implementation idea: borrowable token bucket — tenants can borrow up to X tokens which are repaid over a repay_window (e.g., 1h). Risks: billing reconciliation and abuse.
alex: Finance note: we can't give open-ended credits. Proposals: (1) cap borrowable by tier, (2) higher overage rate for borrowed tokens, or (3) require prepay for certain tiers. Also need metrics: credit_consumed, credit_repaid, grace_events.
sarah: Infra: doable with current rate-limiter with small extension. Two options: A) leaky/burst bucket with smoothing_window param, B) separate smoothing middleware that converts bursts to queued requests. Pref A for predictability. Example config snippet we can start from:
```
quota_policy:
  smoothing_window_sec: 300  # 5m
  borrowable_tokens: 500
  repay_window_sec: 3600  # 1h
  max_borrow_ratio: 0.2
```
This keeps changes localized.
emily: UX: Console needs a new toggle/slider: "Burst grace" with explanation and preview of impact on billing. Add a small banner in tenant usage view that shows "Grace used: 120 tokens". AC: users can opt-out and see exact token accounting.
jules: Also call out perf ACs — smoothing must not silently increase tail latency. Suggest SLO: 99th pct <= 500ms for interactive paths; background jobs can be queued.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: created issue #3421 — "smoothing-policy: initial spike handling" (assigned to dmitri). :white_check_mark:
maya: Next steps: dmitri to collect traffic samples by EOD Wed, jules+emily to draft PRD and UI mocks by Friday, alex to propose pricing guardrails by Friday. Sync Thu 11:00am (calendar invite incoming). Owners assigned in thread. Thanks everyone. :rocket:
